heroHeadline: Constitutional Amendment to Remove Sulyok Underway; EU Funds Milestone Clock Ticking
heroSubtitle: PM Péter Magyar's government formally launched constitutional amendment proceedings on June 1 to create a framework for parliamentary removal of President Tamás Sulyok and Prosecutor General Gábor Bálint Nagy, both of whom refused May 31 resignation deadlines. The amendment — the second use of Tisza's 141-seat supermajority — is expected to pass within one month. The €16.4 billion EU funds deal signed May 29 now enters implementation: Hungary must meet 27 super-milestones by August 31, 2026, for first disbursements in Q4. Hungary formally notified NATO on May 28 it will not supply weapons to Ukraine. Hungary's Q1 2026 GDP growth reached +1.7% — its fastest pace in four years — while inflation fell to 2.1% in April, reflecting post-transition economic confidence. On May 30, Budapest hosted the UEFA Champions League Final at Puskás Aréna (PSG 4-3 Arsenal), and the Magyar government blocked CATL's planned Debrecen expansion.
footerNote: Tracker covers Hungary's political transition from Orbán's 2010 return to power through the 2026 post-election transition. Data reflects publicly available reports from verified sources.
